transcript.content: Hello. What brings you to the clinic today?
I'm here because I've been struggling with episodes where I eat unusually large amounts of food. When this happens, I feel a complete loss of control and feel like I just can't stop myself.
After these episodes of overeating, do you do anything to try to prevent weight gain, such as making yourself throw up, fasting, or exercising excessively?
No, I don't do any of those things to try to prevent weight gain. I've never made myself throw up, fasted, or tried to exercise excessively after these episodes.
How often do these episodes of overeating typically occur, and how many months or years has this been going on?
This has been going on for about a year and a half now. On average, I have these episodes at least once a week, and it has been happening at that weekly frequency for at least the last 3 months.
During these eating episodes, do you experience things like eating much faster than normal, eating until you feel uncomfortably full, or feeling very guilty or disgusted with yourself afterward?
I'm not quite sure if I eat faster than normal or until I feel uncomfortably full. But I definitely feel extremely guilty and disgusted with myself after it happens.
Do you often find yourself eating these large amounts of food even when you don't feel physically hungry, or do you tend to eat alone because you feel embarrassed by how much you are eating?

I'm not really sure about the hunger part, but I definitely eat alone because of how embarrassed I am. I feel so much shame about the amount of food I'm consuming that I make sure no one else is around to see me. It's just really hard to admit that.
Do these episodes of overeating cause you significant distress or interfere with your daily life and relationships?

Yes, they cause me a massive amount of distress and have really impacted my social life. Afterward, I feel incredibly depressed, guilty, and disgusted with myself, which leads me to isolate and eat alone out of embarrassment.
When you finish one of these eating episodes, do you ever feel physically bloated, stuffed, or to the point of physical discomfort?

I don't really experience extreme physical discomfort or bloating after these episodes. Honestly, I haven't paid much attention to how my body physically feels because I'm usually just so overwhelmed by the guilt and shame.
When you have these episodes, do you find yourself consuming the food very quickly, almost like you are rushing, compared to how you normally eat?
I'm not really sure about that, to be honest. I haven't paid close attention to the speed at which I'm eating during those episodes because I'm just so overwhelmed by the feeling of losing control.
Do you ever find yourself starting these eating episodes even when you have recently eaten a full meal or when your stomach doesn't feel empty at all?
I'm not really sure about that, to be honest. I haven't really noticed whether my stomach feels empty or if I've recently eaten when these episodes start.
Have you ever used laxatives, water pills, diet pills, or any other medications to try to prevent weight gain after these eating episodes?
No, I've never used laxatives, diet pills, or any other medications to prevent weight gain. I don't take anything like that after these episodes.
